title: Daylight
tagline: A city's sunrise and sunset curves for a whole year. Read its latitude, longitude and daylight saving time, then pin it on the map.

title: Profile
tagline: Slice the Earth along a hidden straight line. Read the elevation profile, then guess where the line is and which way it points.

title: Sky Over
tagline: A star chart from a mystery city. Polaris's height is the latitude; where the celestial equator crosses the meridian, minus Greenwich sidereal time, is the longitude.
sources: HYG Database v4 (merged Hipparcos / Yale / Gliese catalog)

title: Figure-Ground
tagline: One square kilometer of streets, white on black, with no labels. From the texture of the street net, name the city.

title: Watershed
tagline: A river's whole drainage basin, reduced to an unlabeled outline. Name the river.

title: Parallel
tagline: Five cities, one reference. Tap every one that lies farther north. Yes, Rome is north of New York.

title: Great Circle
tagline: Draw the shortest flight path between two cities on a Mercator map. The smaller the area between your line and the true great circle, the higher your score.

title: Drift
tagline: The first 10 days of a real ocean drifter's track are drawn. Follow the current and mark where it will be on day 90.
sources: NOAA Global Drifter Program (AOML): 6-hour quality-controlled tracks

title: Aftershock
tagline: Every earthquake in the world that day is on the map except the biggest one. Find where it struck, then guess how big it was.

title: Forecast Match
tagline: Five cities, five weather cards from yesterday. Match each temperature curve and sunrise time to its city.
sources: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (ERA5, offline snapshot)

title: Intersection
tagline: Several streets meet at one junction. From the street names alone, name the city.
Here is a year of 311 complaints from one NYC ZIP code. Pin that neighborhood on the map.
sources: NYC Open Data · 311 Service Requests from 2020 to Present
NYC Open Data · Modified Zip Code Tabulation Areas (MODZCTA)

title: Fare
tagline: A real NYC yellow-cab trip: pickup zone, dropoff zone and time of day. Guess the metered fare and how long it took.
sources: NYC TLC Yellow Taxi Trip Records 2023 (NYC Open Data)

title: Grade
tagline: Three real violations from one NYC restaurant inspection. Guess the total points, then the letter grade in the window.
sources: NYC Open Data · DOHMH Restaurant Inspection Results
NYC Health · Restaurant grading and scoring

title: Turnstile
tagline: A New York subway station's 24-hour entry curve, weekday vs. weekend. Read the rhythm of the crowd and name the station; misses are measured in stops.
sources: MTA Subway Hourly Ridership: Beginning 2025 (NY Open Data)

title: Bridge Count
tagline: Given one day's weather, guess how many cyclists crossed the four East River bridges: rank the bridges, then estimate the total.
sources: NYC DOT Bicycle and Pedestrian Counts (ct66-47at)
NYC DOT Bicycle and Pedestrian Count Sensors (6up2-gnw8)

title: Rat Race
tagline: Two New York ZIP codes: which one failed more rat inspections this month?

title: Cuisine Mix
tagline: What does a ZIP code's restaurant mix look like? Read its flavor fingerprint, then pin the neighborhood on the NYC map.

title: Year Built
tagline: Three photos of New York buildings. Read the windows, materials and ornament to guess the year each was built.
sources: Wikidata SPARQL (year built P571, coordinates, image P18)
NYC PLUTO tax-lot data (NYC Open Data; used to cross-check year, floors and use)

title: Isochrone
tagline: Every station you can reach in 30 minutes from one subway stop forms an isochrone. Read its shape and pin where it starts.

title: Then Price
tagline: What did a dozen eggs cost in March 1983? Travel back to a past month and guess the price of three everyday items, scored by percent error.
sources: BLS Average Price Data (downloaded via FRED)
BLS public API: CPI-U all items (CUUR0000SA0)

title: Old Menu
tagline: A century-old menu: given the restaurant, the year and one dish's price, guess what three other dishes cost.
sources: US CPI-U monthly index (datasets/cpi-us, from BLS)

title: Unlabeled
tagline: A US macro curve with the axes removed and only the recessions shaded. Name the indicator, then date the decade.

title: Shock Date
tagline: Four market lines, one hidden date: which day did the shock hit?
sources: FRED: VIX, Treasury yields, WTI crude, exchange rates
Yahoo Finance: S&P 500, Nasdaq, gold futures

title: H-1B
tagline: A real H-1B Labor Condition Application (LCA): given the job, employer and city, guess the annual salary it reports.
sources: US DOL OFLC LCA Disclosure Data
h1bdata.info (mirror of public LCA data, filings submitted in 2024)

title: Contract
tagline: A real US federal contract description. Guess its dollar value, scored on a log scale.

title: Duty Free
tagline: An absurdly specific line from the US tariff schedule. Guess its import duty rate.

title: Concurrent
tagline: Five 24-hour Steam player curves, five games. Match them: time-zone peaks and popularity give them away.

title: Rent Index
tagline: Guess a US county’s 2-bedroom Fair Market Rent (HUD FMR), then settle four higher-or-lower duels.
sources: HUD Fair Market Rents FY2026 (county level)

title: Basket
tagline: A year and $20. Shop at that year's real grocery prices and spend exactly all of it. A knapsack puzzle with history.

title: Food Web
tagline: Six species, 15 pairs. Decide who eats whom and draw the food web, scored by edge F1.

title: Phenology
tagline: One species' weekly sightings across a year in one country. Name the species, then predict when it peaks in another country.

title: Ingredients
tagline: The label read backwards: start with the tiniest ingredients and name the food.

title: Genome Size
tagline: Guess how big this species' genome is. From viruses to lungfish it spans more than seven orders of magnitude, scored on a log scale.

title: AQI Rank
tagline: Rank five cities by yesterday’s PM2.5, from dirtiest to cleanest. Your only clue is the two weeks before.

title: Tide
tagline: Three days of a harbor's tide curve. Guess the port. Only one high tide a day? Think Gulf of Mexico.

title: Landfall
tagline: The track of a historic hurricane, ending more than a day before landfall. Predict where it comes ashore and pin it on the map.

title: Transit Dip
tagline: A star's brightness dips because a planet passed in front of it. Read the depth of the dip and estimate how big the planet is.

title: Gravity Assist
tagline: Today's real planet positions are laid out in front of you. Leaving Earth, is it cheaper to fly direct or to slingshot off another planet? Rank the routes by fuel.
sources: NASA JPL “Approximate Positions of the Planets” (Keplerian elements, 1800-2050)

title: Ground Track
tagline: A satellite's ground track over 12 hours. Tell whether it is ISS / Starlink, polar, GPS, Molniya or geosynchronous.

title: Ngram
tagline: An English word's frequency curve in books from 1800 to 2019. Guess the word; semantic similarity tells you how close you are.

title: Cognates
tagline: The same word in six languages, farthest from English first. Guess the English word.

title: First Use
tagline: Here is an English word and its meaning. Guess the year it first appeared in written English.

title: Spike
tagline: The Wikipedia article that surged hardest two days ago, shown only as a nameless pageview curve. Each wrong guess reveals another article that spiked the same day.
sources: Wikimedia Pageviews API: daily top list
Wikimedia Pageviews API: per-article daily views

title: Dialect Pin
tagline: The dialect quiz played backwards: read how someone says soda or pop, and guess which US state they grew up in.
sources: Harvard Dialect Survey (Bert Vaux & Scott Golder, 2003)
State result text mirror at asucbi/BDSR2

title: Old News
tagline: A snippet of real old-newspaper OCR text with no date and no masthead. Read the language and the news, then guess the year it was printed.

title: Sitelinks
tagline: How many languages of Wikipedia cover a topic? Rank 5 topics, then estimate one number.

title: Toponym
tagline: You get the literal meaning of a place name, such as “Black Pool”. Find the place on the world map.
sources: Etymology sections of Wikipedia place articles

tagline: Definitions from Webster's 1828 dictionary with the word itself blacked out. Guess the word.
sources: Webster's 1828 American Dictionary (CSV transcription, public domain)
google-10000-english word list (used to pick common words)

title: Heatmap
tagline: Every episode's IMDb rating of a TV show, laid out as a season × episode heatmap. Read the ups and downs and name the show.

title: Chart Run
tagline: A song's week-by-week rank curve on the Billboard Hot 100. Guess the year first, then the song.

title: Palette
tagline: A famous painting boiled down to five dominant colors. Guess the year it was painted and its movement.
sources: Art Institute of Chicago API (public-domain paintings, CC0 metadata)

title: Lineage
tagline: A royal family tree with every name blacked out, leaving only birth and death years and sex. Name the dynasty.
sources: Wikidata Query Service (family P53, father P22, mother P25, titles P39/P97, continents of citizenship P27/P30)
Wikidata entity search API (resolving well-known dynasties)

title: Popular Move
tagline: In the same chess position, the move 1500-rated players play most often is often not the one 2500+ players play most. Can you tell them apart?
sources: Lichess open database (1500 band: January 2014 standard games)
Lichess Elite Database (2500+ band: Dec 2021, Jan 2022)

title: World Record
tagline: The progression of one game’s speedrun world record, reduced to times and years. Guess the game.

title: Tour Map
tagline: Every stop of a tour drawn on a map, with no names and no years. Name the artist first, then the year.

title: Weight
tagline: Read a board game's blurb, mechanics and play time, then guess its BoardGameGeek complexity rating (1–5).
sources: TidyTuesday 2022-01-25 · BGG blurbs, mechanics and player counts

title: Funded
tagline: A Kickstarter pitch: goal, backer count and blurb are all laid out. Guess what percent of its goal it ended up raising.

title: Ratio
tagline: You get only the flour : liquid : fat : egg ratio. Name the dish.

title: Who Lives Here
tagline: A resident answers only with Census numbers. Ask five questions, then pin their neighborhood on the US map.

title: Time Use
tagline: How many minutes a day does a group of Americans spend on an activity? Estimate three, using their sleep and participation rate as clues.
sources: BLS ATUS time series files (tu.series / tu.data)

title: Trajectory
tagline: A country's 200-year path across the income × life expectancy chart. Read the route and name the country.
sources: Gapminder World (GDP per capita, PPP, inflation-adjusted)

title: Splits
tagline: A real marathoner's splits for the first 25 km. Predict the finish time. Spotting who will fade is the skill.

title: Pyramid
tagline: Read the population pyramid. Name the country.
sources: World Bank Open Data (SP.POP.*.FE/MA, from UN World Population Prospects)

title: Commute Mode
tagline: Given a US county, guess how many commuters take transit, bike, or work from home.
sources: U.S. Census Bureau, ACS 5-year 2019–2023, Table B08301 (Means of Transportation to Work)
U.S. Census Bureau, ACS Table B01003 (Total Population)

title: Life Table
tagline: What are the odds that a 40-year-old man or woman in a given country and year reaches 80? Use life expectancy and other clues to estimate the percentage.
sources: UN World Population Prospects 2024 — Abridged Life Table (Medium variant)

title: Holiday
tagline: A full year of public holidays with every name hidden. Read the dates and guess the country.
sources: Nager.Date Public Holiday API (2026, "Public" holidays only)

title: Grid Mix
tagline: One day of hourly generation by fuel for a US grid region. The duck curve, hydro and nuclear baseload all give it away.
sources: EIA-930 Hourly Electric Grid Monitor (Balance half-year files)

title: Garage
tagline: The ten most-registered car brands in one New York county. Read the garage, guess the county.
sources: NY DMV Vehicle, Snowmobile, and Boat Registrations (data.ny.gov)

title: Commit Log
tagline: Five real commit messages. Guess which open-source repository they came from.

title: Star History
tagline: The weekly new-star curve of a GitHub repo. Guess the repo from its shape.
sources: GH Archive (WatchEvent), via the github_events table on the public ClickHouse playground
GitHub REST API (repo metadata: language, creation date, topics, total stars)

title: CVSS
tagline: A real vulnerability description with the vendor and weakness names blacked out. Guess its CVSS base score, then its weakness type (CWE).

title: Tagged
tagline: Top-voted Stack Overflow questions with the tags removed. From the title alone, pick the real tags out of 10 candidates, scored by Jaccard overlap.

title: Wayback
tagline: A homepage from the Internet Archive with the brand and images scrubbed out. Name the site, then the year.
sources: Internet Archive Wayback Machine CDX API

title: Pwned
tagline: Two common passwords. Which one shows up more often in data breaches?
sources: Have I Been Pwned: Pwned Passwords range API

title: Front Page
tagline: Four Hacker News stories from one day. From the title, domain and comment count alone, guess how many points each earned.

title: Subdomain
tagline: Subdomains from a hidden company's newest TLS certificates: vpn, sso, jira… Name the company.

title: Stack Trace
tagline: Real error stacks pasted into GitHub issues: guess the language, and which framework or library it tripped over.

title: Changelog
tagline: One line from an open-source changelog with the name blacked out. Guess the software, then the year it shipped.

title: Departures
tagline: Every nonstop destination from one airport. Work out which airport it is from the pattern.

title: Headway
tagline: A rhythm game whose beats are the real scheduled arrival times at one New York subway platform.

title: Ship Lane
tagline: A crop of European shipping-density heat map. Name the strait, sea or port.

title: Rail Time
tagline: Two stations and the distance between them. How long does the fastest scheduled train take? US, Canada, Germany and France.

title: Snowplow
tagline: A real snowstorm over a real street grid. Plan your plow route to clear every main road, as fast as you can.
sources: NOAA GHCN-Daily daily snowfall (NCEI Access Data Service)

title: Sail
tagline: Study a real wind field over the sea and set up to 5 waypoints to sail across the strait as fast as you can.
sources: Open-Meteo Historical Forecast API (yesterday's wind, live)
Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (ERA5 reanalysis, snapshot fallback)

title: Ticker Runner
tagline: A side-scrolling runner whose terrain is one trading day of a US stock index: grab coins on the rallies, jump the spikes on the sell-offs.

title: Topo Golf
tagline: A real patch of Earth's terrain shrunk to a putting green. Read the slopes, sink the putt, then guess where in the world it is.
sources: Esri World Shaded Relief / Gray Canvas basemaps

title: Quake Defense
tagline: Tower defense where the enemies are yesterday’s real earthquakes and magnitude sets HP. Build a 10-cell lane and hold the line.

title: Storm Run
tagline: Fly a courier through real radar echoes: draw the lowest-risk route across yesterday’s US weather radar.
sources: Iowa Environmental Mesonet: NEXRAD N0R US composite archive

title: Levee
tagline: Storm rain falls on real terrain. Place three levees to keep as many real buildings dry as you can.

title: Paint a Million
tagline: On a population-density map, paint the smallest area that holds exactly one million people.

title: Interrogate
tagline: Twenty questions about a hidden country. Ask in your own words; answers are computed from World Bank data.

title: Missing Number
tagline: A data news brief with three numbers blanked out. Read the numbers that are left and fill in the gaps.

title: Real or Synthetic
tagline: Four trend lines, three forged by an algorithm from the real thing's statistics. Spot the genuine one.
sources: NOAA / NASA global monthly temperature anomaly (datasets/global-temp)
EIA Brent and WTI crude oil prices (datasets/oil-prices)
EIA Henry Hub natural gas price (datasets/natural-gas)

title: Described
tagline: A text-only GeoGuessr: read a description of a street photo, with no picture, and drop a pin on the world map.

title: Spurious
tagline: Six real yearly curves, and only one pair has a correlation above r = 0.9. Find it.

title: Data Connections
tagline: Sixteen items hide four groups, each sharing one real Wikidata statement. Find them.

title: Spotter
tagline: A real plane-spotter photo: name the airport first, then the airline, the aircraft type and the season.

title: Trainspotter
tagline: A railway photo: name the operator and the train type, then pin where it was taken.
sources: Wikimedia Commons train-type categories (photos, coordinates, authors, licenses)
